facts.value: Check with staff.mobility@ul.ie to see if funding is available. Funding is allocated on a first come basis.
5 working days excluding travel time
Identify the organisation you will visit and obtain permission from the organisation as well as your line manager.
Discuss the type of activities you wish to undertake and create a programme of activities in collaboration with the host organisation.
Complete the Staff Mobility agreement for Teaching or Training.
The partner institution will sign your agreement, your line manager signs off on the quality of the agreement and grants permission to travel.
Please do this at least 5 weeks prior to your intended travel date.
Submit your fully signed mobility agreement to staff.mobility@ul.ie and UL Global will sign the agreement regarding the administrative requirements.
Allow 10 working days for your contract to be issued.
80% of your grant payment will be made within 30 calendar days after the signature of the agreement by both parties.

Keep your boarding cards and submit copies of these along with a signed and stamped Certificate of Attendance from your host to staff.mobility@ul.ie within 10 days of your return from teaching/training.
Complete the final report which you will receive via email from a Europa.eu email address.
Your final grant payment will be made within 10 working days on receipt of all documentation.
Once your final grant payment is made, you must complete the Acknowledgement of Grant Receipt form and return the completed form to staff.mobility@ul.ie.
Please check out the process map by downloading it here.
You must register your travel as part of Erasmus+ Staff Mobility for Teaching or Training.

facts.value: If you are interested in completing an Erasmus+ EU Staff Training mobility, attending a Staff Week organised by one of UL's partner universities may be a good option. Staff Weeks are usually designed to give an overview of the host university's institution and departments, while bringing together teaching and non-teaching staff to share ideas and potentially establish connections for future collaboration.

facts.value: Incoming staff wishing to participate in Erasmus+ Staff Teaching or Training activities must be individually accepted by a staff member in the host department who is responsible for organising the teaching and/or training activities.
Acceptance is dependent on the participant, the sending institution, and the host department at the University of Limerick.

Agreement for hosting staff members is dependent on agreeing in advance to the contents of the teaching/training plan, the timing of the mobility, and the presence of a signed Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreement.
Potential visiting staff members will need to contact the relevant department in the first instance.
